column1: Response
The chatbot explains difficult concepts in simpler language when I get stuck.
I use it after class to review topics at my own pace.
It gives me quick feedback on practice questions.
The step-by-step examples make long assignments less overwhelming.
I like asking follow-up questions without feeling embarrassed.
It helps me translate unfamiliar terms before I read the course material.
The practice questions are useful, but some answers repeat the same idea.
I can study late at night when a tutor is not available.
It helps me plan an essay, but I still write the final draft myself.
I learn more when the chatbot asks me to explain my reasoning.
Sometimes it sounds confident even when the answer is wrong.
I have seen it invent sources, so I check citations myself.
I worry that relying on it too much will weaken my problem-solving skills.
It is tempting to copy an answer instead of working through the question.
I want clearer guidance from instructors about acceptable AI use.
I do not want to share private details from class discussions with a chatbot.
My internet connection is unreliable, so I cannot always use it.
It helps me understand instructions written in English.
Audio explanations would make the tool easier for me to use.
I prefer feedback from my teacher when the topic is personal or sensitive.
The chatbot saves time on routine questions, leaving more time for group work.
My study group compares its suggestions with our notes before trusting them.
I would use it more if it showed why each answer was suggested.
It is most helpful as a starting point, not as the final authority.
